requirement_structuring.structuring_summary: The requirement is fully resolvable. The lexical ambiguity regarding the direction of the integration action ('add') is resolved by the glossary definition of 'downstream systems' as entities receiving events from System-A. The requirement is structured as a single functional requirement.

source_fragments: System-A must add System-B to their downstream systems and allow System-C to subscribe to the Reporting flow.

fields.action: configure System-B to receive events from System-A and allow System-C to subscribe to the Reporting flow

structured_requirements.final_statement: System-A shall configure System-B to receive events from System-A and allow System-C to subscribe to the Reporting flow.
structuring_notes: The phrase 'add System-B to their downstream systems' was interpreted based on the glossary definition: 'downstream systems' are external systems that receive events from System-A. Thus, 'adding' implies configuring System-B as a consumer.
The phrase 'allow System-C to subscribe to the Reporting flow' was retained as a distinct action within the same functional requirement as it describes a capability provision by System-A.
